name: Fourierism
summary: Fourierism, from Charles Fourier, holds that society should be reorganised into voluntary self-governing associations (phalanxes) of about 1,620 people in which work is varied and attractive, members share in the product as co-proprietors and the passions are satisfied rather than repressed. It rejects commerce, the wage system, the isolated household and governmental or revolutionary politics, and aims to spread by the example of a trial community. It guarantees a minimum and the right to work while keeping unequal shares of capital, labour and talent.
scope: The founding doctrine of Charles Fourier as a utopian socialist programme of voluntary associations (phalanxes), drawing on his writings as published on the Marxists Internet Archive. It excludes later communes and Marxist or anarchist appropriations. Many modern questions are inferred and marked low confidence.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Fourier called for wages high enough to end poverty and a decent minimum, but he proposed abolishing wages in favour of dividends, so a legal minimum wage is only loosely related.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Fourier attacked commerce and its middlemen as wasteful and parasitic and wanted producers to sell collectively; he equally distrusted government action, so this is a rejection of the market half of the claim.

public-ownership.rationale: Phalanx capital is held as exchangeable shares by members and investors, not by the state, and Fourier dismissed governmental action as unable to secure the good.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Harmony keeps unequal wealth, with capital earning a fixed share of profits; Fourier proposed no punitive taxation, but he never discussed taxation directly.

property-fundamental.rationale: Harmony explicitly rejects any general community of goods and keeps individual accounts and shares, though Fourier also put the right to work and a minimum ahead of property.

cut-welfare.rationale: Fourier insisted on a decent minimum for those unable to work and called the right to a minimum a first right of man, so cutting welfare is opposed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Members are co-proprietors who hold shares and receive 5/12 of profits for labour, though investors who do not work also hold capital shares, so ownership is not exclusively the workers'.

strong-leader.rationale: Fourier held that any administration prefers its own good to the people's and expected change from voluntary example, not from a leader overriding gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Fourier called belief in governmental action a ridiculous prejudice and never appealed to legislation or coercive power, though he kept a loose world congress of phalanxes and never called himself anti-state.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.

reviewHistory.rationale: Fourier believed global association would end war and replace military armies with industrial armies, so more military authority runs against his programme.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.

decide-locally.rationale: Society was to be built from self-governing phalanxes spreading by example from localities to nations, with only loose coordination at world level.

traditional-family.rationale: Fourier treated the isolated household as wasteful and marriage as potentially harmful to women, and replaced both with communal living and shared domestic work.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Fourier held that women's condition reflects the social order and that roles should follow aptitude, not sex; he did not frame gender in modern terms.

gradual-change.rationale: He expected association to spread gradually by the force of example from a trial phalanx, but he also rejected established institutions as part of Civilization.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about other international bodies (such as the EU, WTO, IMF or WHO) or about support, funding or reform without enforcement powers, and the statement now asks whether the UN should have powers to enforce its decisions against member states.

reviewHistory.rationale: He envisaged a world body, later called a World Congress of Phalanxes, to coordinate associations globally.

free-trade.rationale: Fourier criticised commerce as the source of evil and wrote against economic liberalism and free exchange, though he also wanted global harmony.

nation-first.rationale: Fourier expected global association to remove war and national rivalry, so putting national interest first is opposed.

limit-growth.rationale: Fourier expected cooperation to greatly raise production and to reclaim land; limiting growth is contrary to his tone.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Fourier was a utopian believer in productivity gains from association and large works, but he put social organisation ahead of technology.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): the old wording asked whether revolution is sometimes justified, and this disagreement rested on a preference for reform or lawful means, which doesn't say revolution is never justified.

reviewHistory.rationale: Fourier rejected governmental and revolutionary politics and expected the new order to spread by voluntary example without force.

experts-over-public.rationale: Early Phalanx government is a regency of those with the most capital, industrial and scientific knowledge, advised by an industrial council.

central-planning.rationale: Associations are voluntary, and Fourier denied that government action could establish the good; planning is by phalanx councils, not a central state.

socialized-markets.rationale: Phalanxes were to sell goods collectively and exchange with each other, a kind of association-owned market, but the statement is not framed in his terms.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Fourier kept inheritance, holding a child's legacies in trust until adulthood, so heavy taxation is not part of the scheme.

basic-income.rationale: Fourier asked for a guaranteed minimum as a first right of man, but tied to the right to work and provided by association, not an unconditional state payment.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Fourier dismissed governmental action and relied on shareholder associations deciding on investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Association members each hold exchangeable shares in the Phalanx in proportion to their contribution, spreading ownership among many rather than a state or a few owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wages are replaced by dividends, but the Phalanx keeps shares, accounts and exchange, so money persists.

one-party-rule.rationale: He rejected political action and coercion altogether and expected change by voluntary association.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He rejected the idea that any government secures the good, and monarchy was one of the forms of Civilization he criticised; not directly stated.

democracy-best.rationale: Fourier ridiculed constitutional machinery such as the balance of powers and ministerial responsibility, though he did not oppose popular rule outright.

workers-councils.rationale: Government is by a regency and industrial council of series officers within voluntary associations, not councils replacing parliaments.

natural-rulers.rationale: The regency goes to those with most capital or knowledge and capable women, implying a fitness-based leadership, though not a doctrine of natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Fourier relied on peaceful example, expected association to end war, and never proposed coercion.

war-builds-character.rationale: He expected industrial armies to replace military ones and association to eliminate war.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Fourier believed in a divine order but derived it from his own science of the passions, not scripture.

military-superiority.rationale: He wished to end war and military armies, so superiority over rivals is not a goal.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He envisioned world association, though his own antisemitism complicates this; not directly addressed.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Fourier saw history as phases of social order and sought harmony between capital, labour and talent within the Phalanx, not class war.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Harmony divides profit among labour, capital and talent, so incomes remain unequal, though poverty is abolished.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Fourier held that the God-given passions should be satisfied, not repressed, and that interest and attraction drive work, so self-regarding motives are legitimate.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He rejected the repression of the passions by Civilization and held that satisfaction of the passions leads to harmony, which puts individual attraction first.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He held that Civilization is a social plague, though he welcomed industry in Harmony.

restore-past-order.rationale: Fourier rejected the existing order of Civilization and was oriented to a new future harmony, not a lost one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He presented his system as a social science and wanted a trial phalanx to prove it by results.

direct-action.rationale: He wanted change by founding model communities rather than by elections, which resembles direct action, though non-confrontational.

means-match-ends.rationale: He sought to found the harmonious society by voluntary peaceful association.

return-to-foraging.rationale: He held that industry, cooperation and large-scale works would raise production.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Fourier carried the subdivision of tasks to the extreme, but his short rotating work sessions meant no one was tied to one occupation, which Engels praised, so the answer splits.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution is by labour, capital and talent, with a minimum.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Fourier criticised the wage system as exploitative but kept profit and capital returns in the Phalanx, so adherents reject the claim as a universal truth.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Fourier rejected governmental and revolutionary politics as ridiculous and sought peaceful association.

collective-farming.rationale: Series of agrarians farm collectively in the Phalanx.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He saw commerce as the source of evil and association as ending war.

harm-principle.rationale: He defended sexual freedom as long as no one is abused.

individual-rights-only.rationale: He criticised abstract rights and focused on the right to work, which is realised in association, so a strictly individualist rights view is rejected.

conscription.rationale: He wanted military armies replaced by voluntary industrial armies, so compulsory military service is opposed.

positive-liberty.rationale: Fourier said the first right of man is the right to work and to a minimum, as abstract rights are empty without material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: He mocked scholars as the uncertain sciences, but did not address media power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Fourier held that character types are spread across all, with passions common to humanity, so group ability differences are not his view; his own prejudices were not hereditarian.

total-state.rationale: Fourier held governmental action cannot establish the good and never appealed to legislation or coercion.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He expected association to end war and replace military armies, so conquest is opposed.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority in the Phalanx rests on contribution and function, not oaths of loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: Fourier built the system on freely chosen, attractive labour and condemned repugnant, forced work.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: He claimed to have discovered a science of passions and social order, so he treated knowledge as objective.

universal-morality.rationale: He believed in a divine social order and universal passions found in all people, discoverable by his science.

single-common-good.rationale: Fourier sought a single harmony in which all passions combine, worked out by his science of association.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Fourier late in life supported Jewish emigration to Palestine with Rothschild assistance.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Late in life Fourier supported Jewish emigration to Palestine, so he accepted a form of return, though not from a rights theory.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Members move among groups and series by choice and share in the proceeds, giving workers a stake and voice, though the regency is chosen by contribution.

economic-freedom.rationale: Fourier objected to state action, but he also attacked free exchange and commerce, so he would not link freedom to markets; weak inference.

rule-by-example.rationale: Fourier relied on the force of example from a trial phalanx rather than law or coercion to spread his order.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Fourier grounded his system in God and in passion, not reason alone, though he claimed a science.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: He wanted a decent minimum guaranteed to all who cannot work, with no citizenship test mentioned.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He tied the minimum to the right to work, so able people were to work, though work was to be attractive and provided.

class-collaboration.rationale: Labour, capital and talent share profits; collaboration within phalanx.

workers-nation.rationale: His association was meant to be worldwide and cross-class, not organised nationally by class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Fourier held that important jobs should be open to women on skill and aptitude and treated women as individuals.

ban-interest.rationale: Capital invested in the Phalanx earns 4/12 of profit, so a return on lending is accepted in his scheme.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He saw government as self-interested rather than class tool.

national-mission.rationale: Fourier wanted his model to spread by example to all, but not as a national mission of any country.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Engels credits Fourier that women's emancipation measures general emancipation.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He held every administration prefers its own good.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He held that governmental action cannot establish the good and left social organisation to associations, so a minimal state is nearer than an active one.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Fourier held that everyone has the same twelve common passions and should have a place in Harmony, and he treated women as individuals.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not his vocabulary; he expected association to spread from locality to nation to world by example.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Fourier thought government is self-interested and cannot create the good, so a stronger socialist state is the opposite of his path.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Association was voluntary and to spread by free adoption, so legitimacy rests on consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Fourier condemned commerce as the source of evil, so competing for exports is not his goal.

population-transfer.rationale: Fourier proposed forcing Jews into farm work, but not transfer.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Fourier never appealed to coercive power and wanted association to spread peacefully and end war.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Fourier built in friendly rivalry between series and groups, but his system aims at harmony and cooperation, not struggle between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: He distrusted state power and political machinery; banning parties would be an act of government he did not endorse.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: He held that the right to work and a minimum frees people from dependency on others, which resembles non-domination, though he did not use the term.

separated-powers.rationale: He dismissed the balance of powers and ministerial responsibility as devoid of sense.

vanguard-party.rationale: Fourier rejected political action and held that people would adopt association by example, not through a leading party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Fourier considered poverty the main cause of social disorder and proposed high wages and a decent minimum.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Fourier blamed poverty on Civilization's social order and its disorder, not on population growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Harmony depends on combining 810 character types, so variety strengthens his association.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Phalanx offices go to the most capable and highest contributors, not by chance.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Fourier disliked state regulation and preferred association to eliminate middlemen and speculation.

party-controls-media.rationale: Fourier rejected coercive government and political parties as vehicles of the good.

party-commands-army.rationale: He aimed to replace armies with industrial armies and abolish war, so a party-commanded military is contrary.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: He rejected political parties as means and individual attraction as the engine of association.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He wished to abolish military force, so command arrangements are not his concern; mild rejection.

church-by-bishops.rationale: He criticised organised religion as corrupt and offered no role for episcopal governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Fourier criticised organised religion as corrupt and advised no government by clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: He opposed war, so workers refusing to support their government's war would fit, though he did not argue it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Fourier held that suppressing the passions is the defect of Civilization, so censorship for virtue is opposed.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Phalansteries house members in shared buildings rather than family homes, which contradicts universal family ownership.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Phalanxes are agricultural-industrial communities in the countryside, and he proposed reviving land.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Fourier ranked Civilization as a lower stage than Harmony, so he does not hold that all civilizations are equal.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Fourier held that Civilization's repression distorts the passions, and Harmony needs 810 distinct character types.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: He hated bankruptcy and speculation but favoured the poor; weak inference.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He argued that political reform leaves the poor at the palace gate, so political change without economic change is empty.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Fourier held that freedom of the passions produces productivity, so restriction cuts against it.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He wanted global association to end poverty everywhere, but not by aid.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: He rejected general community of goods but treated the right to work and a minimum as primary, so property serves that end.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Fourier distrusted state action and did not propose state control of churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: He distrusted party politics, but the Phalanx has no head of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He rejected coercion in forming and keeping associations.

sacred-ruler.rationale: He held that governments prefer their own good to the people's and dismissed rulers as a source of the good.

flat-income-tax.rationale: No income taxation is discussed; Harmony divides profit by fixed shares.

character-from-environment.rationale: Fourier held that 810 character types are given by God and merely suppressed by Civilization, so adherents combine innate passions with environmental distortion.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He held rulers act in their own interest and dismissed checks as ineffective, but he did not propose lawless rulers.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a goal in his writings; earthly harmony and reclamation of the planet are.

mixed-constitution.rationale: He ridiculed the balance of powers and constitutional design as useless.

leader-cult.rationale: He distrusted rulers and relied on voluntary example.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: He sought class harmony, not continued struggle.

land-redistribution.rationale: Association is voluntary and based on shares, with no confiscation of estates.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Fourier wanted world association spreading by example and no war, so territorial claims on behalf of kin abroad do not fit; he never addressed the question.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: He rejected coercion and criticised organised religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: His emphasis on free expression of passions and sexual liberty makes compulsion opposed, though he never addressed dress.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: His unity was global and voluntary, not ethnic.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Fourier late in life backed Jewish emigration to Palestine rather than assimilation in France, so he did not take this view.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Fourier read history as phases of social order driven by passions and institutions, which partly overlaps with materialism but not fully.

ban-cartels.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its own rationale does not support its value under the reworded statement: it cites nationalisation or no state prohibition, not a ban on cartels.

reviewHistory.rationale: He attacked commerce's speculators and monopolisers but looked to association, not state prohibition.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: He wanted offices open to women on skill and aptitude, not quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Fourier's association was meant to be global, and he condemned commerce, but he did not propose imperial economic blocs.

moral-incentives.rationale: Fourier relied on attraction and passions plus dividends, with higher pay for repugnant work; he did not rely on moral appeals.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: He rejected force and revolution and sought change by example.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Rank in Harmony follows contribution, not birth, but he did keep inheritance.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a civilization, a region or Eurocentrism rather than the student's own nation, which is all the statement now asks about.

reviewHistory.rationale: He used "civilization" pejoratively and sought universal harmony.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a civilization, a region or Eurocentrism rather than the student's own nation, which is all the statement now asks about.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He spread association by example, and rejected Civilization as a stage to be exported.

patriotic-education.rationale: Education was built on developing children's passions and industrial instincts.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Engels reports Fourier saw Civilization in a vicious circle, producing the opposite of its aims.

delink-world-market.rationale: He wanted universal association, not autarky among poor countries.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He called abstract equality of rights impractical, preferring the concrete right to work and a minimum.

elective-rulers.rationale: Phalanx regency seats go to the largest contributors; no elections are described.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He dismissed constitutional checks and politics, and relied on example.

parliament-supreme.rationale: He called constitutional balance and ministerial responsibility devoid of sense.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Fourier gave animals a role in Harmony and predicted transformed nature; not clearly stated about suffering.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Poor members in the Phalanx receive an advance, and the rich invest in association, but this is not framed as duty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: He rejected political action and wished to found new communities instead.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Fourier criticised commerce and Civilization's parasitic middlemen, loosely supportive.

native-born-offices.rationale: He favoured universal association over nativism.

party-own-road.rationale: Each community would form by example in its own way.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He wanted worldwide association of capital and labour.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: His known concern was the subordination of women and the sexual order, not male disadvantage, so adherents would give it little priority.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He held that the phalanx was a universal solution suited to all peoples.

military-guardian-role.rationale: He wished to replace armies with industrial armies and abolish war.

paid-care-work.rationale: Domestic work is shared in the Phalanx and remunerated as labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Phalanx children dine apart from parents, and from age 4.5 own their earnings.

office-by-exam.rationale: Offices go to the largest contributors, not exam winners.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: He saw marriage as potentially harmful to women and defended sexual freedom, so ending a marriage freely follows.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: He provided collective guarantees via the Phalanx, though individual accounts exist.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land is held by the Phalanx but shares are owned by members.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Fourier criticised parasitism but celebrated refined pleasures and luxury, so adherents are split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: He wished to end war and rely on peaceful example.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: He expected much larger populations in Harmony and valued children.

job-guarantee.rationale: Fourier held the first right of men is the right to work, guaranteed under Guarantism, but by association rather than government.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: He held government prefers its own good, but he never taught disobedience.

local-production.rationale: Phalanxes were meant to be largely self-supplying communities of farmers and artisans.

informal-organisation.rationale: Phalanx has a formal structure of series and groups.

religious-nation.rationale: He sought universal harmony, not religious nationhood.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Harmony rejects general community of goods and keeps individual accounts.

defeat-communism.rationale: He opposed community of goods but not by force.

religion-illusion.rationale: Fourier started from the existence of God and a divine social order, though he attacked organised religion, so he would deny that religion is mere consolation.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Fourier used "Civilization" pejoratively and condemned commerce, though Engels credits his sharp critique.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Engels reports that Fourier made women's emancipation the measure of general emancipation, within a new social order.

socialized-care.rationale: Children raised in tribes and domestic work shared.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Fourierism is built on voluntary associations of about 1,620 people in phalansteries governed by series and groups.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He rejected Civilization and commerce but also any general community of goods.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Fourier late in life supported Jewish emigration to Palestine.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: He defended same-sex attraction as long as no one was abused.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Fourier held that change comes by example without legislation or coercive power, and criticised governments for serving themselves, so suppression of opposition is rejected.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He criticised organised religion and rejected coercion.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Members move among groups and series, but governance is by regency.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: He connected poverty and women's subordination, loosely.

alienated-labor.rationale: He saw wage work in Civilization as repugnant and designed attractive labour to remove it; Wikipedia notes it would eliminate what Marxists call alienation.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He started from God and a divine order, but not authority.

social-market-economy.rationale: Fourier wanted commerce replaced by association, not tamed by social protection within the market, so this compromise is not his.

rich-first.rationale: He saw poverty as the main cause of disorder.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Fourier assigned 4/12 of Phalanx profits to invested capital, so capital earns a return, which departs from credit at cost; the topic itself is only loosely related.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Fourier linked women's liberation and a reclaimed nature, loosely.

reification.rationale: Engels credits his critique of the gap between phrases and reality.

racial-franchise.rationale: He foresaw a universal association of peoples and wished to end sectional rule; a racial franchise is contrary, though his own antisemitism complicates it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: He rejected organised religion's corrupt forms.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Fourier argued that political rights mean little to the poor at the gates of the rich, and made the minimum a first right.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: He defended same-sex attraction if no one is abused, so he would not exclude gay people, though he sought to abolish armies.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Fourier began from belief in God and a divine order and rejected coercive state action, so a state atheism campaign is opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He believed disorder arises from thwarted passions and poverty, and Harmony ends crime by satisfying them; he did not discuss abolition of institutions.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: He distrusted both philanthropy and state; his answer is association.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: He opposed traditional marriage as potentially harmful to women and treated women as individuals, so shared authority is closer to his view than male headship.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Fourier rejected drill and coercion; his education rested on attraction and varied work, not national service.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Fourier's phalanx divides the product among labour, capital and talent, roughly 5/12, 4/12 and 3/12, so ownership of capital earns income; he condemned idle traders and speculators but not returns to capital.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Fourier sought harmony between classes through shared dividends and rejected revolutionary politics, so working-class political power as the test of socialism is not his framing.

second-chamber.rationale: He rejected governmental politics, constitutions and political reform, so a legislative second chamber is not part of his scheme.

municipal-property.rationale: Members of a phalanx are co-proprietors, which is local and collective, but shares stay unequal and tied to individual capital, so it is neither plainly municipal nor private ownership.

family-wage.rationale: Fourier proposed replacing the wage system with dividends divided among capital, labour and talent, so a family wage is not the mechanism he favoured.

dense-cities.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on preferring villages or the countryside, on land use, or on reasons other than the environment, and the statement now asks only whether dense cities produce lower greenhouse-gas emissions per resident than suburbs.

reviewHistory.rationale: The phalanstery housed some 1,620 people in one large building in place of isolated households, an early form of compact communal living.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Fourier never addressed armed forces in this way; his harmony rests on voluntary association rather than coercion, but he left no view on who may bear arms.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Fourier rejected revolutionary and governmental politics and expected reform by the example of a trial phalanx, so violently smashing the state runs against his method.

sacred-nation.rationale: Fourier's cosmopolitan harmony and universal association are at odds with a sacred nation; he focused on the phalanx and humanity, not national community.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Fourier wrote nothing on regional exploitation inside states; his critique was of commerce and civilisation generally, not of centre and periphery.

workers-own-party.rationale: Fourier rejected governmental and political action as a remedy for poverty and expected reform by example of a trial phalanx, so a workers' party in politics runs against his method.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Fourier held that women's emancipation measures social progress, and shares in a phalanx go to capital, labour and talent regardless of sex.

premarital-sex.rationale: Fourier's doctrine held that the passions, including amorous ones, should be satisfied rather than repressed, and he attacked conventional marriage morality.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Fourier rejected the isolated owner and made the phalanx a joint-stock association where capital, labour and talent each earn a share, so land is not owned by the first worker.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Fourier built his system on a self-devised science of passions and attacked the moral philosophers and civilised religion's repression of passions, rather than scriptural authority.

national-church-status.rationale: Fourier attacked civilised religion and moral repression and wanted free association of passions, so a legally privileged national church is contrary to his system.

simple-living.rationale: Fourier explicitly rejected asceticism and austerity; the phalanstery aims at luxury, abundance and the satisfaction of the passions.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Fourier held that civilisation takes away the natural rights of gathering, pasture and hunting, and so owes the poor a guaranteed minimum as compensation.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Fourier argued that the degree of women's emancipation measures social progress and he condemned marriage as servitude, and Engels credits him with this critique.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Fourier rejects governmental politics and relies on association rather than law, but nothing in the sources addresses natural-law claims about unjust law.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Fourier divides the product among capital, labour and talent, so labour alone is not the source of value.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Fourier rejects governmental and revolutionary politics and expects association to spread by example, so a party-led system is foreign to it.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Fourier insisted on a decent minimum for those unable to work and called the right to a minimum a first right of man, so cutting welfare is opposed. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Work should be organised so that each person moves between varied tasks chosen according to their own inclinations.
missingStatements.rationale: Attractive labour, with workers changing tasks about eight times a day among groups they choose, is the core of Fourier's scheme.
missingStatements.declined: Covered in part by abolish-division-of-labor, where Fourier answers against abolition; too specific to the Fourierist scheme to ask everyone.

missingStatements.text: Women's emancipation is the measure of a society's general emancipation.
missingStatements.rationale: Engels credits Fourier as the first to declare that the degree of women's emancipation is the natural measure of general emancipation.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Fourier and Engels's attribution; women-equality-needs-economic-change and patriarchy-structural already cover the contested ground.

missingStatements.text: Social reform should be pursued by founding model communities that others can copy, not by legislation.
missingStatements.rationale: Fourier never appealed to legislation or coercive power, and expected associations to spread by the force of example from a trial phalanx.

notes: Fourier's writings also contain antisemitic passages (economic and religious in kind, per Wikipedia). Adherents may split on inheritance and on his sexual and cosmological claims. Many modern-policy answers are low-confidence inferences.
